title: BJP drops Hardeep Puri, Smriti Irani in fresh UP Rajya Sabha slate of 8
excerpt: The BJP announced an entirely new slate for the October 16 biennial elections to ten Rajya Sabha seats from Uttar Pradesh, with no sitting member renominated and two Union ministers left out.
body:
• The BJP on October 5 announced eight candidates for the October 16 Rajya Sabha biennial elections from Uttar Pradesh, dropping all sitting members — including Union Petroleum Minister Hardeep Singh Puri and Union Minister of State BL Verma.
  • The eight nominees are Dharampal Singh, Radhakant Ojha, Prakash Pal, Vidyasagar Sonkar, Gopi Krishna Pandey, Priyanka Singh Rawat, Ram Pratap Singh Chauhan and Shruti Gangwar — with two women and a caste mix of three OBCs, two Brahmins, two Dalits and one Thakur.
  • Puri's exclusion has triggered speculation of a Union Cabinet reshuffle; the 74-year-old is the only Sikh member of the Council of Ministers.
  • What this means for you: if you follow Uttar Pradesh politics — and lakhs of NRIs from the state do — this is a full generational reset with no incumbent renominated, a slate clearly calibrated for the 2027 assembly election. Polling is October 16, with the BJP set to win seven seats comfortably and a contest likely for the tenth.

A clean sweep of the sitting MPs

The Bharatiya Janata Party has named an entirely new set of eight candidates for the biennial elections to the Rajya Sabha from Uttar Pradesh, scheduled for October 16. The list, approved by the party's Central Election Committee and announced on Monday by BJP leader Tarun Chugh, contains not a single renomination.

https://x.com/ndtv/status/2107109035157962858

Among those dropped are Union Petroleum Minister Hardeep Singh Puri and Union Minister of State BL Verma, whose terms end in November. Sitting members Arun Singh, Brijlal, Neeraj Shekhar, Geeta Shakya and Seema Dwivedi were also left out, along with Dinesh Sharma, who vacated his seat after being appointed Lieutenant Governor of the Andaman and Nicobar Islands.

Context & Background

The eight nominees — Dharampal Singh, Radhakant Ojha, Prakash Pal, Vidyasagar Sonkar, Gopi Krishna Pandey, Priyanka Singh Rawat, Ram Pratap Singh Chauhan and Shruti Gangwar — reflect a deliberate balancing act. Two are women: former Lok Sabha member Priyanka Singh Rawat and Shruti Gangwar, daughter of eight-time MP and Jharkhand Governor Santosh Gangwar. Dharampal Singh, an OBC leader and minister in Chief Minister Yogi Adityanath's cabinet, is among the better-known faces.

The timing matters. The announcement came a day before the October 6 deadline for filing nominations, and just months before the Uttar Pradesh assembly elections expected early next year. With the BJP expected to comfortably win seven of the ten seats on its own assembly strength, the list doubles as a signal to the party's caste and regional constituencies ahead of that larger battle.

Impact & Analysis

The biggest talking point is Puri. At 74, he is the only Sikh member of the Union Council of Ministers after Ravneet Bittu's term expired in June, and his exclusion has set off speculation about an impending cabinet reshuffle. Reports earlier had linked a possible renomination to the 2027 Punjab elections and the party's Sikh outreach — calculations that now appear to have been overtaken.

Smriti Irani, the former Union minister and Amethi MP who was made BJP national general secretary, was also widely tipped as a possible pick but did not make the list. The BJP's approach — zero incumbents, new organisational faces — suggests the leadership preferred a slate built for the assembly election campaign over rewarding existing parliamentarians.

The arithmetic for the ten seats is settled in broad strokes. The BJP-led NDA commands 288 votes in the 403-member assembly (255 BJP MLAs plus allies), with 37 first-preference votes needed per seat. The Samajwadi Party, with 101 MLAs, has nominated Ram Gopal Yadav and Dhanraj Parimal Nathwani and can win two seats. The tenth seat could see a contest if the SP fields a third candidate, reviving the cross-voting drama of the 2024 election, when the BJP forced a contest despite only having the numbers for seven.

Diaspora Angle

Uttar Pradesh sends the largest bloc to the Rajya Sabha, and the Upper House shapes legislation that directly touches the diaspora — from emigration and citizenship rules to the fiscal bills that set remittance and investment terms. For the large UP-origin community abroad, Puri's exit is the number to watch: whether he stays in the cabinet without a parliamentary seat, and who takes the petroleum portfolio, will ripple into energy prices and policy. Nominations close October 6, scrutiny is on October 7, withdrawals run till October 9, and polling happens October 16 from 9 am to 4 pm with counting the same evening.

What's Next

Watch the nomination filings on October 6 for any surprises from the SP on the tenth seat — a third SP candidate would force a contest and test cross-party loyalties. Then watch the cabinet: with two Union ministers now without a Rajya Sabha berth, a reshuffle looks increasingly likely before the assembly election season begins.
